svg.text: Why bulk can differ from the approved sample
1. Material batches — a later lot than the sample was cut from
2. Colour across a long print run — density and registration wander
3. Humidity and season — board takes on moisture from the air
4. Hand finishing vs machine production — samples are made slowly
5. Tolerance stacking — component tolerances add up at assembly
• Two identical sealed samples — one with the buyer, one at the factory
• The signed specification travels with the sample
• Photographs of the sealed sample under agreed lighting
• The acceptance standard stated in the order, before production
Colour acceptance, stated up front: ΔE ≤ 2.0 against the approved sample, grey scale grade 4.
The inspection at receiving is run against the buyer's own sealed copy — not a photograph or a recollection.
